title: ResponseEntity and HTTP status codes
summary: Set a response status, headers and optional body.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: ResponseEntity in Spring Boot in Hindi | Handling HttpStatus while creating REST API

richText: An HTTP response has a status code, headers and an optional body.
ResponseEntity<T> lets a controller choose all three. T is the body’s Java type.
ResponseEntity does not convert the body itself. Spring’s message converters still write the response format.

1: The request succeeded. A body can contain the result.
The request created a resource. Location can identify its URL.
The request succeeded with no response body.
The request lacks valid authentication credentials.
The server refuses the requested operation.
The resource was not found or the server does not reveal it.
The request conflicts with the current resource state.
An unexpected server failure prevented completion.

richText: @PostMapping does not set 201 automatically. Choose a status from the operation’s result.
Do not attach a response body to 204.
Do not return 200 with an error message when the request failed.

example.title: Return a found resource or create a new one
description: These methods belong in a @RestController mapped to /journal.
journalService is an injected service. JournalResponse and CreateJournalRequest are application DTOs.
findVisible returns Optional<JournalResponse>. create returns the saved DTO with an ID safe to use as a path segment.
The service applies ownership rules and performs persistence; those implementations are not shown.
explanation: A found result produces 200 and the JournalResponse body.
An empty Optional produces 404 without a body.
created(location) produces 201 and a Location header. body(saved) adds the saved DTO.
If the saved ID is 42, Location is /journal/42.
This code chooses HTTP responses; request validation is covered separately.

richText: Keep response data separate from stored data
A response DTO declares the fields the API returns.
Return only fields the caller should receive. Database entities can contain internal data that the API should not expose.
Keep shared error response rules in exception advice rather than repeating them in each handler.
